newsitem.title: USA: CBOT chairman Arbor re-elected to third term.
newsitem.headline: CBOT chairman Arbor re-elected to third term.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) chairman Patrick Arbor has been re-elected to head the exchange for a third two-year term, the CBOT said on Wednesday.
Arbor, the 60-year-old principal of trading firm Shatkin, Arbor, Karlov & Co, would become the longest serving chairman in the exchange's history, a CBOT spokesman said.

"I am deeply grateful to the members of the Chicago Board of Trade for their confidence in me as well as their support of our initiatives," the spokesman quoted Arbor as saying. "Many challenges lie before us -- challenges which we will continue to transform into opportunities."
Arbor was running opposite John Gilmore, a partner at Goldman Sachs & Co and one-time CBOT chairman in the 1980s.
The exchange also said Richard Sandor, chairman of Center Financial Products Ltd, was elected as CBOT second vice chairman. He will serve a two-year term.
The CBOT added that five full-member directors were elected to serve for three years.

They are independent traders Ann Berg and Charles Carey Jr, LIT Investor Services senior vice president Gordon Linn, Iowa Grain Co vice president and secretary Jack Frymire and Lehman Brothers Inc executive vice president Charles Nastro.
For a three-year term as associate member director, Paul Johnson, vice president of Quantum Financial Services Inc, was elected, CBOT said.

For CBOT's full member nominating committee positions, Richard Durra of Durra Grain Co and Alaska Commodities Inc president Jerry Manne were elected. Independent trader John Kelley will be an associate member on the committee.
